results.title: How to delete(or kill) the current word in emacs? - Stack Overflow
results.snippet: The Emacs way to remove the word one is inside of to press M-backspace followed by M-d. That will kill the word at point and save it to kill ring (as one unit). If the cursor is at the beginning or after the end of the word, only one of the two is sufficient.

results.title: GNU Emacs Manual - Commands for Human Languages
results.snippet: Kill back to the beginning of a word (backward-kill-word). M-@. Mark the end of the next word (mark-word).(If you wish to kill only the next word but not the punctuation before it, simply do M-f to get the end, and kill the word backwards with M-DEL.) M-d takes arguments just like M-f.

results.title: Words - GNU Emacs Manual
results.snippet: M-d (kill-word) kills the word after point. To be precise, it kills everything from point to the place M-f would move to.(If you wish to kill only the next word but not the punctuation before it, simply do M-f to get the end, and kill the word backwards with M-.)

results.title: GNU Emacs Manual - Killing and Moving Text
results.snippet: Kill word (kill-word). See section Words. M-DEL.Commands that kill backward from point add text onto the beginning. This way, any sequence of mixed forward and backward kill commands puts all the killed text into one entry without rearrangement.
